243	### 1.11 PHI và dữ liệu nhạy cảm: định nghĩa và phạm vi
244	
245	Accessed 2026-11-08. Sources:
246	
247	- Regulation text: 45 CFR 160.103, 164.308, 164.314, 164.501, 164.502, 164.504, 164.514. Read on
248	  eCFR via its official API, as of 2026-11-01 (**local check**: `curl --compressed`, HTTP 200).
249	- Anthropic: the BAA help article and the [hipaa-setup](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hipaa-setup)
250	  page.
251	- AWS: the HIPAA eligible services reference.
252	- NIST CSRC glossary.
253	
254	**Source gap:** the HHS.gov HIPAA pages (Privacy Rule summary, business associates, cloud computing
255	guidance, de-identification) returned **HTTP 403** to both WebFetch and curl (**local check**). I
256	could not read them, so every claim below rests on the regulation text that HHS administers. The
257	HHS links are given for human readers, marked 📖.
258	
259	#### 1.11.1 Definitions
260	
261	| # | Finding | Marker | Source |
262	|---|---|---|---|
263	| 1.11.1.1 | **Health information** is any information, "oral or recorded in any form or medium", that (1) "is created or received by a health care provider, health plan, public health authority, employer, life insurer, school or university, or health care clearinghouse" and (2) "relates to the past, present, or future physical or mental health or condition of an individual; the provision of health care to an individual; or the past, present, or future **payment** for the provision of health care to an individual." | ✅ | [45 CFR 160.103](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-45/section-160.103) |
264	| 1.11.1.2 | **Individually identifiable health information** is "a subset of health information, **including demographic information** collected from an individual", that is created or received by a provider, health plan, employer or clearinghouse, relates to health, care or payment as above, **and** "(i) that identifies the individual; or (ii) with respect to which there is a reasonable basis to believe the information can be used to identify the individual." | ✅ | [45 CFR 160.103](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-45/section-160.103) |
265	| 1.11.1.3 | **PHI** is "individually identifiable health information" that is transmitted or maintained by electronic media or "in any other form or medium". Four things are excluded: FERPA education records, records described at 20 U.S.C. 1232g(a)(4)(B)(iv), "employment records held by a covered entity in its role as employer", and information about a person "deceased for more than 50 years". **ePHI** is the electronic subset. | ✅ | [45 CFR 160.103](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-45/section-160.103); HHS summary 📖 [Privacy Rule summary](https://www.hhs.gov/hipaa/for-professionals/privacy/laws-regulations/index.html) (403, not read) |
266	| 1.11.1.4 | **Covered entity** means "(1) A health plan. (2) A health care clearinghouse. (3) A health care provider who transmits any health information in electronic form in connection with a transaction covered by this subchapter." A health plan includes "a health insurance issuer". | ✅ | [45 CFR 160.103](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-45/section-160.103); 📖 [HHS covered entities](https://www.hhs.gov/hipaa/for-professionals/covered-entities/index.html) (403) |
267	| 1.11.1.5 | A **business associate** is a person who, on behalf of a covered entity, "creates, receives, maintains, or transmits protected health information" for a regulated function, "**including claims processing or administration, data analysis, processing or administration** … billing, benefit management". The term also covers "a subcontractor that creates, receives, maintains, or transmits protected health information on behalf of the business associate." | ✅ | [45 CFR 160.103](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-45/section-160.103) |
268	| 1.11.1.6 | **Payment** includes "adjudication or subrogation of health benefit claims", "billing, claims management, collection activities … and related health care data processing", and "review of health care services with respect to medical necessity, coverage under a health plan". | ✅ | [45 CFR 164.501](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-45/section-164.501) |
269	| 1.11.1.7 | **De-identified** information is not individually identifiable, so it is not PHI. Under the safe-harbor method it counts as de-identified only if 18 identifier types are removed, including names, address parts smaller than a state, dates other than the year, phone and email, "(G) Social security numbers", "(H) Medical record numbers", "(I) Health plan beneficiary numbers", "(J) Account numbers", "(K) Certificate/license numbers", URLs, **IP addresses**, full-face photos, and "(R) Any other unique identifying number, characteristic, or code". The covered entity must also have no "actual knowledge" that the rest could identify the person. (The other method is an expert determination; not read in detail.) | ✅ | [45 CFR 164.514(a)–(b)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-45/section-164.514); 📖 [HHS de-identification guidance](https://www.hhs.gov/hipaa/for-professionals/special-topics/de-identification/index.html) (403) |
270	| 1.11.1.8 | **Minimum necessary:** when using or disclosing PHI, a covered entity or business associate "must make reasonable efforts to limit protected health information to the minimum necessary to accomplish the intended purpose". | ✅ | [45 CFR 164.502(b)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-45/section-164.502) |
271	| 1.11.1.9 | **PII** is not a HIPAA term: the seven HIPAA sections downloaded contain no occurrence of "personally identifiable" (**local check**: `grep -c -i`, 0 in each). The US federal definition (OMB Circular A-130, used in NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5) is "information that can be used to distinguish or trace an individual's identity, either alone or when combined with other information that is linked or linkable to a specific individual". NIST SP 800-122 lists medical, educational, financial and employment information as examples of linked information. | ✅ | [NIST CSRC glossary: PII](https://csrc.nist.gov/glossary/term/personally_identifiable_information) |
272	| 1.11.1.10 | **PHI vs PII (inference from 1.11.1.1–1.11.1.9):** PII is defined by **identifiability alone**. PHI needs **three things together**: identifiable, about health, care or payment for care, and created or received by a covered entity, or held by a business associate on its behalf. So most PHI is PII, but most PII is not PHI. An identifier such as an ID number or a bank account number becomes part of PHI when it sits in the same record as health or claim information held for a covered entity. | ⚠️ inference (no source states this comparison; derived from the definitions above) | — |
273	| 1.11.1.11 | **Does HIPAA apply to Papaya at all?** HIPAA's definitions refer to US law: a "health insurance issuer" must be "licensed to engage in the business of insurance in a **State**". Papaya serves insurers "across SEA and Asia" (`work/00-challenge.md`). Whether any Papaya tenant is a HIPAA covered entity, and so whether Papaya is a business associate, is a **legal question I cannot answer**. This file follows the brief, which lists HIPAA as a compliance requirement, and treats Papaya as a business associate of its insurer clients: claims processing on their behalf matches 1.11.1.5. | ✅ (definition text) / ⚠️ (applicability: needs Papaya legal) | [45 CFR 160.103](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-45/section-160.103) |
274	| 1.11.1.12 | **Regional law** (for example Vietnam, implied by "CCCD"): I could not find and read an official government source this session for how local law classifies health data, national ID and bank data. Secondary sources (law-firm and advisory sites) say Vietnam's Personal Data Protection Law (No. 91/2025/QH15) took effect on 2026-01-01, with Decree 356/2025/NĐ-CP replacing Decree 13/2023/NĐ-CP, and that health data and some financial data are "sensitive personal data". **Not verified. Do not use it in `docs/` until it is read in the official text** (Topic 5). | ⚠️ (secondary sources only) | e.g. [EY legal alert, Decree 356/2025](https://www.ey.com/vi_vn/technical/tax/tax-and-law-updates/nghi-dinh-so-356-2025-nd-cp-quy-dinh-chi-tiet-mot-so-dieu-va-bien-phap-thi-hanh-luat-bao-ve-du-lieu-ca-nhan) (not official) |
275	
276	#### 1.11.2 Which group each Papaya data type falls into
277	
278	This applies 1.11.1 to the data the brief names. The legal text is ✅; **applying it to Papaya is
279	my inference (⚠️)**, because I have not seen Papaya's schemas or contracts. It assumes the HIPAA
280	framing of 1.11.1.11.
281	
282	| Data (code from `work/01-problem-framing.md`) | Group | Why (rule) |
283	|---|---|---|
284	| Medical records, medical documents (MED) | **PHI** | Relates to "physical or mental health or condition" and identifies the member (1.11.1.1–1.11.1.3) |
285	| Diagnoses (MED) | **PHI** | Same rule as medical records |
286	| Claim history (MED) | **PHI**, even without a diagnosis | Claims are "payment for the provision of health care" (1.11.1.1, 1.11.1.6) |
287	| National ID / CCCD (NID) | **PII** on its own. **Part of PHI** when it is in a member or claim record | An identifying number. Safe harbor lists "(R) any other unique identifying number" (1.11.1.7); "(G) SSN" is the US equivalent |
288	| Bank account (BANK) | **PII** (financial) on its own. **Part of PHI** when it is the payout account of a claim | "(J) Account numbers" is a listed identifier (1.11.1.7), and claim payout is payment for care (1.11.1.6) |
289	| Policy and member numbers | **Part of PHI** in claim context | "(I) Health plan beneficiary numbers" (1.11.1.7) |
290	| Same data, de-identified by safe harbor | **Not PHI** | 1.11.1.7. Under local law it may still be personal data (1.11.1.12, ⚠️) |
291	| Infrastructure metadata (resource names, metrics, config without customer values) | **Neither** | Provided it carries none of the 18 identifiers. **Caution:** IP addresses, URLs with IDs, and object keys that contain names or ID numbers are identifiers (1.11.1.7) |
292	
293	**Practical consequence (inference ⚠️):**
294	- Claim records combine MED with NID and BANK, so any production store or stream that carries claim
295	  data should be treated as PHI-bearing as a whole: Aurora claim tables, the claim-documents S3
296	  bucket, and the queues and logs of claim services.
297	- Separating PII from PHI field by field is not a safe basis for agent access.
298	
299	#### 1.11.3 Conditions for a model provider (or any vendor) to process PHI
300	
301	| # | Finding | Marker | Source |
302	|---|---|---|---|
303	| 1.11.3.1 | A covered entity may let a business associate "create, receive, maintain, or transmit" PHI only after it "obtains satisfactory assurance that the business associate will appropriately safeguard the information". A business associate may do the same with a **subcontractor**, after it obtains the same assurances. The assurances "must be documented through a written contract or other written agreement" (the BAA). The Security Rule has the same requirement for ePHI. | ✅ | [45 CFR 164.502(e)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-45/section-164.502), [164.308(b)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-45/section-164.308), [164.314(a)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-45/section-164.314) |
304	| 1.11.3.2 | Required BAA content includes these duties. The vendor must: not use or disclose PHI beyond the contract; "use appropriate safeguards and comply … with subpart C" (Security Rule); report any use or disclosure not provided for, including breaches; flow the same terms down to its subcontractors; and return or destroy PHI at termination "if feasible". | ✅ | [45 CFR 164.504(e)(2)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-45/section-164.504), [164.314(a)(2)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-45/section-164.314) |
305	| 1.11.3.3 | **Application to Papaya (inference):** if Papaya is a business associate of its insurers (1.11.1.11), any model provider that receives PHI from a Papaya agent is Papaya's **subcontractor**. Papaya then needs a BAA with that provider, and must also check that its own BAAs with insurers allow the subcontracting. | ⚠️ inference from 1.11.3.1 | — |
306	| 1.11.3.4 | **Anthropic BAA scope:** it covers "HIPAA-ready services, such as use of our first-party API, Claude in Microsoft Foundry, or Enterprise plans". "Standard Claude Enterprise plans do not include BAA coverage without action from a Primary Owner." The authoritative list of Eligible Services is the Implementation Guide on the Anthropic Trust Center (not opened). **The Team plan is not mentioned**, so treat Team as not covered (⚠️, confirm with Anthropic). | ✅ (article) / ⚠️ (Team) | [Anthropic: BAA for commercial customers](https://privacy.claude.com/en/articles/8114513-business-associate-agreements-baa-for-commercial-customers) (page shows "Updated over a week ago", no date) |
307	| 1.11.3.5 | **Claude Code under the Anthropic BAA:** terminal and Code tab (local mode) are covered **with the HIPAA configuration** only "when members sign in with their Claude Enterprise account and Claude Code connects directly to Anthropic". A Console API key is "covered through ZDR, not through the HIPAA configuration". The VS Code and JetBrains extensions are **not** covered. Claude Code through Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform, Foundry, Claude Platform on AWS or a Claude apps gateway is **not eligible** for the HIPAA configuration. Connectors, local MCP servers, skills and plugins are available but "not covered". | ✅ | [Anthropic BAA article](https://privacy.claude.com/en/articles/8114513-business-associate-agreements-baa-for-commercial-customers), [hipaa-setup](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hipaa-setup) |
308	| 1.11.3.6 | The HIPAA configuration "doesn't remove cloud provider or GitHub credentials". Data an agent sends to GitHub or another service is **not covered** by the Anthropic BAA. | ✅ | [hipaa-setup](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hipaa-setup) |
309	| 1.11.3.7 | **AWS:** Amazon Bedrock, CloudWatch Logs, S3, Aurora and Lambda are on the HIPAA eligible services list. PHI may be used in them only after "entering into an AWS business associate agreement" (page last updated 2026-10-15). Whether Papaya has an AWS BAA is unknown (⚠️). If Claude Code uses Bedrock, the AWS BAA applies to it rather than the Anthropic BAA; I have **not** verified how far that coverage extends to Claude Code (⚠️). | ✅ (list) / ⚠️ (Papaya status, Claude Code via Bedrock) | [AWS HIPAA eligible services reference](https://aws.amazon.com/compliance/hipaa-eligible-services-reference/) |
310	| 1.11.3.8 | **GCP (Vertex AI, Gemini):** not researched this session. | ⚠️ | — (Topic 5) |
311	| 1.11.3.9 | **Relation to the owner decision (inference):** under the owner's default, PHI never reaches the agent, so none of 1.11.3.3–1.11.3.7 is needed for the DevSecOps agent. `work/01-problem-framing.md` GĐ-9 allows case-by-case approved reads of real data with "BAA/DPA". 1.11.3.4–1.11.3.5 show that on the current Team plan, that exception **cannot include PHI sent to Claude**: no BAA covers it. That would need the separate Enterprise + BAA environment named in the owner decision. GĐ-9 and its consequences should be checked against this when the design is written. | ⚠️ inference | — |
312	
313	#### 1.11.4 Paths by which PHI can reach a DevSecOps agent's context (to handle in Phase 4)
314	
315	**This is my analysis, not quoted from any document.** It lists paths to close or control, so that
316	"PHI never reaches the agent" holds. "Context" includes anything the agent reads: tool output, files,
317	fetched pages, MCP results, images. Anything in context is sent to the model provider and saved in
318	the local session transcript (`~/.claude*/projects/…/*.jsonl`, **local check** on this machine).
319	Controls are only candidates; they are designed in Phase 4.
320	
321	| # | Path | How it gets into context | Why PHI is likely | Candidate controls (Phase 4) |
322	|---|---|---|---|---|
323	| L1 | **Prod logs:** CloudWatch Logs from Lambda and ECS, k0s pod logs, GCP Cloud Logging | Agent runs `aws logs`, `kubectl logs`, or reads a log MCP during debug or incident | Request payloads, exception messages with record values, document-extraction output, IPs (identifier) | Log redaction at source; agent role reads metrics and redacted log groups only; separate log group for raw payloads with no agent access |
324	| L2 | **Database queries:** Aurora prod or replicas | `psql` or a DB MCP; `SELECT *` while debugging; error messages and slow-query or `pg_stat_statements` text with literals | Claim tables hold MED + NID + BANK | No DB credentials for the agent; a schema-only or masked view role; reads of real data only through the GĐ-9 exception |
325	| L3 | **S3:** claim documents, exports, backups | `aws s3 cp/ls`; reading a file to "check format" | Medical documents and ID scans; **object keys** may contain names or ID numbers | Deny `s3:GetObject` on PHI buckets for agent roles; consider whether `ListBucket` exposes keys |
326	| L4 | **Message and workflow payloads:** SQS/DLQ, SNS, Step Functions execution history | Inspecting a DLQ or execution input/output during an incident | Payloads carry claim data; Step Functions stores input/output in history | Same as L3 for `sqs:ReceiveMessage` and `states:GetExecutionHistory`; payloads carry references, not data |
327	| L5 | **Tickets and chat:** Linear, Slack (incl. via MCP connectors) | Agent reads an issue or thread linked from a task | Support escalations paste claim details and screenshots | Ticket hygiene rule (no PHI in tickets); scope or deny those MCP connectors; redaction bot |
328	| L6 | **Partner and member uploaded documents** while debugging prod AI agents (A7b in problem framing) | Engineer gives the agent a failing document to reproduce a bug | The document **is** PHI, and is also an injection vector | Reproduce with synthetic documents; a de-identification step before any document reaches the coding agent |
329	| L7 | **Non-prod data that is not synthetic** | Agent works freely in dev/staging (GĐ-14) | If a prod copy or dump exists in staging, PHI is there | Enforce GĐ-14: no prod → non-prod copies; scan non-prod stores |
330	| L8 | **Repo content:** fixtures, seed files, sample documents, notebooks committed from real data | Agent reads the repo (always) | Engineers copy "a real example" into tests | Secret/PII scanning in CI and pre-commit; review rule for fixtures |
331	| L9 | **CI output:** GitHub Actions logs and artifacts from jobs that touch real data | Agent reads CI logs to fix a failing job | Test or migration output that prints rows | No real data in CI; log masking |
332	| L10 | **What humans paste:** text, screenshots or files pasted into the chat by the engineer | Direct input | Copying from an admin console or a customer email | Training and a clear rule; a `UserPromptSubmit` hook pattern check (weak, advisory) |
333	| L11 | **Prod shell access:** `kubectl exec`, ECS Exec, SSM on EC2 | Agent runs commands inside a prod workload | Env vars, mounted files and local caches hold data or DB credentials | No exec rights for agent roles in prod |
334	| L12 | **Fetched web content:** internal dashboards and admin UIs reachable from the laptop | WebFetch or browser tools | Admin pages show member records | Network or domain allowlist; deny fetch to internal admin hosts |
335	
336	Cross-cutting point (inference): every path above depends on **what the agent's identity is allowed
337	to read**. So the strongest single control for the owner decision is an agent identity with **no
338	data-plane read on PHI stores**: IAM, DB roles and k0s RBAC (Topics 2–3). Redaction and rules on

# 02 — Research: what the tools can actually do today

Purpose: ground every later design decision in current, official documentation, not model memory.
Written in English (it will be quoted in `docs/`); short Vietnamese notes where useful.

## Evidence markers used in this file

This step uses the marker definitions the user set for the research phase (they are slightly
narrower than `CLAUDE.md` Rule 1, where ✅ means "verified in this environment"):

| Marker | Meaning here |
|---|---|
| ✅ | I opened and read the official page in this session; the statement paraphrases or quotes it. Where I also checked something on this machine, the line says **(local check)** |
| 📖 | From official documentation, but I did not open the specific page/section this session (e.g. known only from a link or summary), or the behaviour was not tried |
| ⚠️ | Assumption or inference, not confirmed by a source. Says what is needed to confirm it |

Rules: every claim has a link; no setting or feature name is used unless it appears in the cited
page; access dates are given per topic because these products change weekly.

Process (agreed 2026-11-08, see `CLAUDE.md` Rule 4): each topic is checked by an independent
reviewer subagent; review → fix → re-review until no HIGH/MEDIUM findings remain. Each topic ends
with a short review log.

Local environment for reference: Claude Code `2.1.319` (`claude --version`, **local check**).
Many documented features carry a minimum version (e.g. "requires v2.1.259 or later"); Papaya must
pin a minimum client version (see `requiredMinimumVersion` below).

20:(B) Access authorization (Addressable). Implement policies and procedures for granting access to electronic protected health information, for example, through access to a workstation, transaction, program, process, or other mechanism.
25:(B) Protection from malicious software (Addressable). Procedures for guarding against, detecting, and reporting malicious software.
33:(B) Disaster recovery plan (Required). Establish (and implement as needed) procedures to restore any loss of data.
38:(b)(1) Business associate contracts and other arrangements. A covered entity may permit a business associate to create, receive, maintain, or transmit electronic protected health information on the covered entity's behalf only if the covered entity obtains satisfactory assurances, in accordance with § 164.314(a), that the business associate will appropriately safeguard the information. A covered entity is not required to obtain such satisfactory assurances from a business associate that is a subcontractor.
39:(2) A business associate may permit a business associate that is a subcontractor to create, receive, maintain, or transmit electronic protected health information on its behalf only if the business associate obtains satisfactory assurances, in accordance with § 164.314(a), that the subcontractor will appropriately safeguard the information.
40:(3) Implementation specifications: Written contract or other arrangement (Required). Document the satisfactory assurances required by paragraph (b)(1) or (b)(2) of this section through a written contract or other arrangement with the business associate that meets the applicable requirements of § 164.314(a).
===
 

§ 164.314 Organizational requirements.
(a)(1) Standard: Business associate contracts or other arrangements. The contract or other arrangement required by § 164.308(b)(3) must meet the requirements of paragraph (a)(2)(i), (a)(2)(ii), or (a)(2)(iii) of this section, as applicable.
(2) Implementation specifications (Required)—(i) Business associate contracts. The contract must provide that the business associate will—
(A) Comply with the applicable requirements of this subpart;
(B) In accordance with § 164.308(b)(2), ensure that any subcontractors that create, receive, maintain, or transmit electronic protected health information on behalf of the business associate agree to comply with the applicable requirements of this subpart by entering into a contract or other arrangement that complies with this section; and
(C) Report to the covered entity any security incident of which it becomes aware, including breaches of unsecured protected health information as required by § 164.410.
(ii) Other arrangements. The covered entity is in compliance with paragraph (a)(1) of this section if it has another arrangement in place that meets the requirements of § 164.504(e)(3).
(iii) Business associate contracts with subcontractors. The requirements of paragraphs (a)(2)(i) and (a)(2)(ii) of this section apply to the contract or other arrangement between a business associate and a subcontractor required by § 164.308(b)(4) in the same manner as such requirements apply to contracts or other arrangements between a covered entity and business associate.
(b)(1) Standard: Requirements for group health plans. Except when the only electronic protected health information disclosed to a plan sponsor is disclosed pursuant to § 164.504(f)(1)(ii) or (iii), or as authorized under § 164.508, a group health plan must ensure that its plan documents provide that the plan sponsor will reasonably and appropriately safeguard electronic protected health information created, received, maintained, or transmitted to or by the plan sponsor on behalf of the group h
(2) Implementation specifications (Required). The plan documents of the group health plan must be amended to incorporate provisions to require the plan sponsor to—
(i) Implement administrative, physical, and technical safeguards that reasonably and appropriately protect the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of the electronic protected health information that it creates, receives, maintains, or transmits on behalf of the group health plan;
(ii) Ensure that the adequate separation required by § 164.504(f)(2)(iii) is supported by reasonable and appropriate security measures;
(iii) Ensure that any agent to whom it provides this information agrees to implement reasonable and appropriate security measures to protect the information; and
(iv) Report to the group health plan any security incident of which it becomes aware.

# Set up Claude Code (local mode) for a HIPAA-ready organization

> Prepare developers' computers to run Claude Code (local mode) under the HIPAA configuration. Covers versions, network access, managed settings, and local data.

The HIPAA configuration is an organization setting on Claude Enterprise plans, for organizations that handle protected health information (PHI) and have a [Business Associate Agreement (BAA)](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/8114513-business-associate-agreements-baa-for-commercial-customers) with Anthropic. It applies to Claude Code (local mode) and Cowork (local mode), and it restricts features in both products.

> [!NOTE]
>
> "(local mode)" means a local session, not a [cloud session](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-code-on-the-web.md). Local sessions run in one of these places:
>
> * Claude Code in the terminal
> * Claude Code in the Code tab of Claude Desktop
> * Cowork in Claude Desktop
>
> The Claude Code extensions for VS Code and JetBrains aren't part of (local mode). They keep working with the HIPAA configuration applied, but your BAA doesn't cover them. See the [Implementation Guide](https://trust.anthropic.com/resources?s=l1wrssd9hsbi4gak0tp5a6\&name=%5Banthropic%5D-hipaa-ready-offering-implementation-guide) for the full list of Eligible Services.

This page is for the IT or security administrator who prepares developers' computers. The Primary Owner of your Claude organization applies the configuration itself. [Use Claude Code (local mode) and Cowork (local mode) on a HIPAA-ready Enterprise plan](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/17318731) explains what your BAA includes, how the configuration is applied, and how to schedule the date it's applied.

If members of your organization also use Cowork, follow [Set up Cowork (local mode) for a HIPAA-ready organization](https://claude.com/docs/cowork/hipaa-setup) as well. It covers the Claude Desktop policy and Cowork's local data.

The table shows when to do each part of the setup:

| When | What to do |
| :- | :- |
| Before the configuration is applied | [Prepare computers](#prepare-computers-before-the-hipaa-configuration-is-applied): check how developers connect, update the apps, allow network access, deploy managed settings, and restrict Claude Desktop sign-in |
| After it's applied | The Code tab is off until an Owner turns it back on. [Confirm the configuration on a computer](#confirm-the-configuration-on-a-computer) |
| Ongoing | [Manage local session data](#manage-local-session-data) |

## Prepare computers before the HIPAA configuration is applied

We recommend you start with the tasks in this section and complete them before the configuration is applied.

### Check how developers sign in and connect

The HIPAA configuration takes effect only in sessions where a developer signs in with a Claude Enterprise account and Claude Code connects directly to the Claude API. On any other connection, developers can keep using Claude Code, but it doesn't apply the [HIPAA configuration](#what-developers-see-in-claude-code).

The table shows which connections are eligible. To find out whether your BAA covers a session in a "No" row, see [Use Claude Code (local mode) and Cowork (local mode) on a HIPAA-ready Enterprise plan](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/17318731).

| How Claude Code connects | Eligible for the HIPAA configuration |
| :- | :- |
| A Claude Enterprise account, connecting directly to the Claude API | Yes |
| Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform, Microsoft Foundry, Claude Platform on AWS, or a [Claude apps gateway](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway) | No |
| An [LLM gateway](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway) or any other custom `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` | No |
| `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` or `apiKeyHelper`, on a computer with no Claude Enterprise sign-in | No |
| A Claude Console API key or [federation credentials](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/authentication.md#anthropic-profiles-and-federation-credentials) | No. These sessions belong to a Claude Console organization, which has its own agreement and settings |

#### Check how a computer connects

Open a terminal on the computer, run `claude`, and enter `/status` at the prompt. The **Status** tab shows these lines:

| Line | When it appears |
| :- | :- |
| `Login method` and `Organization` | The session is signed in with a claude.ai account. For a Claude Enterprise account, `Login method` reads `Claude Enterprise account` and `Organization` shows your organization |
| `API provider` | Only when the session uses a cloud provider or a Claude apps gateway |
| `Anthropic base URL` | Only when `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` is set |

If a computer uses a connection that isn't eligible for the HIPAA configuration, you can use [managed settings](#deploy-managed-settings) to block cloud providers, gateways, and credentials set with `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`, or `apiKeyHelper`.

### Update Claude Code and Claude Desktop

The HIPAA configuration requires Claude Code v2.1.285 or later and Claude Desktop v2.19675.0 or later. If your organization uses both the terminal and the [Claude Desktop app](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/desktop.md), update both.

To read the installed Claude Code version, run this command in a terminal. It's the same in Bash, Zsh, and PowerShell:

```bash theme={null}
claude --version
```

A supported installation prints `2.1.285 (Claude Code)` or a higher number.

To read the installed Claude Desktop version, see [Check your version](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/desktop.md#check-your-version).

#### What developers see on an older version

For organizations with the HIPAA configuration, Anthropic's servers reject requests from versions older than the minimum version. Anthropic raises the minimum version over time, and there's nothing for you to configure.

| App | What a developer sees on an older version |
| :- | :- |
| Claude Code | Each request fails with an [`API Error`](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/errors#claude-code-does-not-support-this-model) that says the version is older than the minimum version your organization's policy requires |
| Claude Desktop | An **Update required** dialog that tells the developer to update Claude Desktop to continue using the **Code** tab |

To keep developers on a supported version, [keep Claude Code updated](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/setup.md#update-claude-code). For Claude Desktop, see [Update Claude Desktop](https://claude.com/docs/cowork/hipaa-setup#update-claude-desktop).

### Allow network access

Allow the hosts in this table through your proxy and firewall, over HTTPS on port 443. Allow each whole host, not individual paths.

| Host | Needed for |
| :- | :- |
| `api.anthropic.com` | Claude API requests, telemetry, and the organization policy that tells Claude Code the HIPAA configuration is on |
| `claude.ai`, `claude.com`, `platform.claude.com` | Sign-in and token refresh |
| `sso.claude.com` | Sign-in, when your organization uses single sign-on |
| `downloads.claude.ai` | The native installer and its updates |
| `mcp-proxy.anthropic.com` | [Connectors from claude.ai](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp.md#use-mcp-servers-from-claude-ai) |

This table lists the hosts a native install of Claude Code needs in the terminal to sign in, run, and update. These pages list the rest:

* **Other install methods and optional features**: [Network access requirements](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/network-config.md#network-access-requirements) lists the hosts that npm and Homebrew installs check for updates, and the hosts for features such as plugin installs
* **The Code tab and Cowork**: [Desktop network access requirements](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/desktop.md#network-access-requirements) lists the additional hosts Claude Desktop needs
* **Proxies that inspect TLS**: [Custom CA certificates](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/network-config.md#custom-ca-certificates) shows how to trust your proxy's certificate

Sessions that go through a corporate HTTPS proxy are still eligible for the HIPAA configuration, as long as the proxy can reach the hosts in the table.

Claude Code learns that your organization has the HIPAA configuration by fetching your organization's policy from `api.anthropic.com`, when it starts and again about every hour while the session is in use. The policy is a record of your organization's HIPAA status and the feature restrictions that follow from it.

To check whether one computer has fetched the policy, see [Confirm the configuration on a computer](#confirm-the-configuration-on-a-computer).

### Deploy managed settings

You can use [managed settings](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/managed-settings.md) to direct developers to sign in with a Claude Enterprise account, to block cloud providers and gateways, and to set how many days every computer keeps local session data. The settings apply whether or not the HIPAA configuration is in effect.

The settings in this section are a sample that we recommend as a starting point. Your organization is responsible for deciding what its own environment needs and for confirming that its configuration meets those needs.

The following sample sets four keys that you could add to the [managed settings](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/managed-settings.md#choose-a-delivery-mechanism) your organization deploys:

```json theme={null}
{
  "forceLoginMethod": "claudeai",
  "forceLoginOrgUUID": "xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx",
  "allowedProviders": ["anthropic"],
  "cleanupPeriodDays": 30
}
```

For a fuller `managed-settings.json` with sandboxing, a network allowlist, credential protections, and local data retention, see `settings-hipaa.json` and `README-hipaa.md` in the [settings examples repository](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/tree/main/examples/settings).

#### What each key does

The table shows what to set each key to and what Claude Code enforces for it.

| Key | Set it to | What Claude Code enforces |
| :- | :- | :- |
| [`forceLoginMethod`](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference#forceloginmethod) | `"claudeai"` | Claude Code directs developers to claude.ai sign-in instead of Claude Console |
| [`forceLoginOrgUUID`](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference#forceloginorguuid) | Your organization ID, which an [Owner](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/server-managed-settings.md#access-control) can copy from [claude.ai admin settings](https://claude.ai/admin-settings/organization) | Claude Code exits at startup when the claude.ai sign-in belongs to another organization |
| [`allowedProviders`](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference#allowedproviders) | `["anthropic"]` | Claude Code refuses to start on a cloud provider or a gateway |
| [`cleanupPeriodDays`](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference#cleanupperioddays) | The number of days your records policy lets a computer keep session data | Every computer deletes old session data after the same number of days |

> [!WARNING]
>
> Check the `forceLoginOrgUUID` value before you deploy it. If it doesn't match your organization ID, Claude Code exits at startup for every developer who signs in with a claude.ai account.

The HIPAA configuration doesn't limit `cleanupPeriodDays`, so a developer can raise it in their own settings. When you set it in managed settings, Claude Code ignores the developer's value.

With `forceLoginMethod` or `forceLoginOrgUUID` set, Claude Code also refuses sessions that authenticate with `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`, or `apiKeyHelper`.

#### Confirm the settings loaded
